records.question: What human (man-made) influences threatening coral reefs are listed in the ABSTRACT?
records.ground_truth_answer: The ABSTRACT lists: increased turbidity and siltation; abnormal inputs of nutrients and organic matter; pollution by toxic chemicals and oil; thermal loading; alterations to freshwater runoff; changes in water circulation and wave exposure; direct physical damage and breakage; and the selective removal of organisms or system components producing population imbalances and possibly interfering with nutrient cycling. It also notes that any human use beyond certain levels will alter the system unless compensating actions are taken.
ground_truth_chunks: These resource uses are threatened by many man-made influences, including increased turbidity and siltation, abnormal inputs of nutrients and organic matter, pollution by toxic chemicals and oil, thermal loading, alterations to freshwater runoff, changes in water circulation and wave exposure, direct physical damage and breakage, and the selective removal of organisms or system components producing population imbalances and possibly interfering with nutrient cycling.
Indeed, any human use of a system beyond certain levels will alter it unless compensating actions are taken.

records.question: What was the total number of coral colonies in the 10 resurveyed quadrats in 1980 on the Aua Line (Pago Pago Harbor, American Samoa)?
ground_truth_chunks: The total number of coral colonies in the 10 resurveyed quadrats decreased from 3,670 in 1917 to 2,657 in 1973 and to 1,880 in 1980, perhaps related to the steadily increasing urban impact in the harbor area.

records.question: What was installed in 1980 to aid future surveys of the transects?
records.ground_truth_answer: Fixed markers were installed in 1980 as an aid to future surveys.
ground_truth_chunks: Transects from the shore across the fringing reef to the reef crest were so located with respect to major coastal features that it was possible to reposition the transect line within a few meters on each occasion.
Since some observed variations could be related to inaccuracies in repositioning the transect line, fixed markers were installed in 1980 as an aid to future surveys.

records.question: How many survey sites will be needed in all?
records.ground_truth_answer: At least 10 sites will be needed in all.
ground_truth_chunks: The survey sites have been chosen to represent the major coastal areas around the city, including sites with existing urban impact, sites with expected future impact, and sites up-current and down-current and offshore from the urban area.
At least 10 sites will be needed in all.

records.question: According to the DISCUSSION section, what survey frequency is recommended as the minimum to document changes in variable and fast-growing corals such as *Acropora*?
records.ground_truth_answer: Annual or bi-annual surveys would probably be the minimum necessary to document changes in variable and fast-growing corals such as *Acropora*.
ground_truth_chunks: The appropriate frequency of resurveys has yet to be determined. The studies in Samoa suggest that intervals of several years are too long even to monitor changes in the coral composition of a reef. Annual or bi-annual surveys would probably be the minimum necessary to document changes in variable and fast-growing corals such as *Acropora*. Monthly or quarterly surveys would be needed to relate changes to particular damaging incidents, whether natural or man-made.
